lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Turkish
short: Cast n Chill is a relaxing fishing game where you explore serene lakes, rivers, and oceans. Catch rare fish, upgrade your gear and reel in legendary catches - all with your loyal companion by your side.
about: Cast n Chill's a laid-back fishin’ game for folks who’d rather wet a line than break a sweat. Whether yer driftin’ on a lazy lake, pokin’ 'round a winding river, or droppin’ lines in salty blue water, this here’s a game where you set the pace.           Upgrade Yer Gear  Start with the basics, catch whatever bites, sell your haul, and put those coins toward better rods, reels, and upgrades. Before ya know it, you’ll be wranglin’  rare species  that’d make any angler green with envy.       Explore New Waters  Find yer favourite fishin’ hole or keep wanderin’. There’s  16 peaceful spots to discover , each with its own critters swimmin’ 'round, just waitin’ to bite.          Pick Your Pace  In   Active Mode  , you’re in the thick of it - castin’, reelin’, and keepin’ busy like a loon at nesting time.  Switch to   Passive Mode   if you’d rather let the game do the work while you’re off choppin’ wood.   Set it up on a  second monitor  or  tuck it in the corner  - come back later and see what kind o’ haul the fish gods left ya.          Collect 'Em All  There’s   50+ fish to discover  - some you’ll recognize, some you’ll squint at and go “what in the heck is  that ?” From scrappy little sunfish to big ol’ deepwater beasts, they’re all in the logbook waitin’ for your name.       Legendary Catches  There’s 16 fish out there that still get folks jabberin’ at ol' Rusty's bait shop like they saw Bigfoot ride a moose. Land one, and you'll be part o' the legend.          Boat Buddies  Grab your rod and call a buddy, Cast 'n Chill now has co-op! Whether you’re lookin’ to kick back and fish side-by-side or stir up a bit of friendly competition, it’s all better with company.       Trusty Companion  Nothin’ beats a day on the lake with a four-legged friend. They might not know a spinnerbait from a spoon, but they’ll help you spot a fish - if only 'cause they’re hopin’ for a bite themselves.       Restore Your Very Own Fishing Cabin  Roll up your sleeves and bring a worn down lakeside shack back to life, then kick back and enjoy the quiet while fishin’ off your own dock. Stock your pond, mount replicas of your best catches, and settle in while your trusty companion curls up by the fire.

about: Welcome to Fish to Dish: Idle Sushi! A laid back fishing idler that lives on your desktop, along the bottom of your screen, or just about anywhere else you'd like. Take a moment to ease your mind as you take in the sea breeze, and wait for a bite! In Fish to Dish, you're a fisherman taking to the seas to reel in weird and wonderful creatures of the deep, and then serve them up as sushi. All kinds of customers await, their bellies rumbling... So upgrade your rod, unlock new bait, sail the seas, and even build your own aquarium tank!      • Start a relaxing fishing adventure from the bottom of your desktop screen. Watch as your boat sails the waves, reeling in new fish.   • Play at your own pace, and feel that sense of satisfaction as your boat heaves with awesome catches!Tap your keyboard or click your mouse to speed up the bite and reel in fish even faster!                 • Cast your rod in a range of bays and isles, each with their own unique sea life. You'll see everything from everyday fish, to rare leviathans of the depths.  • What's that floating over there...? Spot starfish, turtles, walruses, even rubber ducks and much more floating out on the waves!  • Fill out your bestiary as you haul in new species, and expand your sushi bar's menu.                         • Prepare your prize catches, and sell a delectable range of sushi dishes to earn gold.  • Level up your sushi bar and spruce it up with furniture and decorations. Make it your own to draw in all kinds of customers, and... cats?                 • Buy rod upgrades to fish more efficiently, and return to shore with a deck chock-full of fish!  • Pick out the right bait for the fish you're after, and reel in elusive rare varieties.                 • Float in relaxation, taking in the joy of fishing as the tides ebb and flow.  • Fill the hatchery with catches, and gaze over your rare fish as they flit within an aquarium ecosystem of your own creation.  • Bid stress farewell, and be at one with nature in Fish to Dish: Idle Sushi. Take time to fish at your leisure!                  Game FAQ   Q:   Screen flickering after Steam pop-up or pressing Shift+Tab? name: Abracademia
lang: English
short: Become a wizard, and a thumping good one! Abracademia is a cozy mage idle life-sim that lives on your screen and keeps you company while you work or play. Pick a coven, manage your daily routine, learn spells, make friends, embark on adventures, and pass exams on your way to graduation.
about: Abracademia is  a cozy witch idle life-sim  that lives on your screen and keeps you company while you work or play.                    Abracademia  runs quietly while you study , watch videos, or play other games.  Your wizard lives their life at your pace. You can micromanage every little detail or let magic handle the rest.    Move Abracademia around the screen, adjust the game speed, or pause anytime you want.                     Your journey begins after you receive your letter from Abracademia School.   Create your own wizard , shaping their appearance, their background, and even their magic wand.    Define a magical profile that reflects who you are,  shaping your strengths, your weaknesses,  and the kind of magic you naturally lean toward.    Finally comes the moment every mage waits for… the  test that determines your Coven.   Will you join the creative Waltzpurgis, the secretive Medusalem, or the outgoing Feynyx?  Each of the five  Covens offers its own unique content and spells.                      Abracademia takes place over five school years, leading up to your wizard’s graduation.  Your character will  attend classes every day, join activities , and, of course, take exams.  While some activities are mandatory, you decide how your wizard spends the rest of each day.    Do you want to be a studious scholar? A gossip queen? A pompous noble, quietly plotting in the shadows?  Or maybe someone who solemnly swears they’re up to no good.     In Abracademia, any path is possible.                     Classes, events, and quests earn you experience in magical disciplines, letting you unlock new spells.   With over 300 spells across 20 disciplines  (Home Magic, Transformative Arts, Umbra…), you can shape your wizard in your own way.  Use magic to get boosts, ace exams, make friends (or enemies), and experiment with different spell combinations to discover crazy synergies.    And if you like a little friendly competition, check the Students Leaderboard!                       Your wizard isn’t alone.  Other students can be rivals, allies… or perhaps something more.   You can study together, attend parties, compete in events, and build relationships that shape your school life.    As your friendships grow, you’ll unlock special quests, and if things go well, you might even end up with someone special in the epilogue!                 When classes are over,  you can dive into quests  and explore the Fabric of Worlds, a place where magical realities meet.  Choose to be a friendly neighborhood wizard, helping wherever you can, or dive into the intrigues of the Magical World and see where they take you!    Quests will reward you with unique items, but they will also test your spell mastery, your friends’ help, and careful stamina management.    Don’t worry, there’s always more than one way to solve a problem.

short: Turn your desktop into a living racetrack with this online idle racing management game. Build your garage, equip parts, and watch your cars run championships on their own. And whenever you like, take the wheel in Driving Mode against up to 20 players.
about: TURN YOUR DESKTOP INTO A LIVING RACETRACK   Desk Top Racer  is an online idle racing management game that lives on a strip of your desktop. Build your garage, prepare your cars, and let the races unfold while you work, study, or play something else. And whenever you like, take the wheel.  TWO WAYS TO PLAY   Automatic mode: you build, they race   The races run on their own. What matters is your strategy: pick the car, equip the parts, look after its condition, and go for the podium.     Tour:  32 countries to conquer, in championships of ten races.     Online races:  rooms of 20 drivers, matched with you by power level.     League:  MMR-based championships once you finish the Tour.     Weather:  six weather types in rotation change who has the edge each day.     Radar:  follow the race, the standings, and the records.     Driving Mode (experimental): now you drive   Accelerate, brake, and take the corners yourself. Cars are the same for everyone: it all comes down to your driving.     Multiplayer:  online rooms with up to 20 real drivers, with qualifying and a starting grid.     Practice:  race against bots on any track you like, with a braking guide line.    Your automatic race keeps running in the background, so you don't miss a thing.    A GARAGE THAT NEVER STOPS EVOLVING  Between one race and the next, there is always something to improve.   Parts, crates, and upgrades     Six part types in six rarities, from Common to Mythic.    Crates come from racing. Drag the part to its slot and watch your performance rise.    Upgrade your parts with no level cap, sell them for Credit, or dismantle them for Scrap.     Mastery, Collection, and Workshop      Mastery Tree:  invest in performance, economy, and automation, such as opening crates automatically.     Mechanical Collection:  complete part sets and earn stats for all your cars.     Workshop:  every car racks up mileage and earns paint points to unlock new colors.     Offline rewards:  keep earning Credit and Mastery even with the game closed.    ALWAYS SOMETHING TO DO     Weekly Missions:  five new missions every week, with DTR Coin as the reward.     Mascots:  ten companions with their own bonuses to win at the Mascot Machine.     TrackCards:  earn each country's card, evolve its rarity, and equip a set with bonuses.     Plincar:  short on Credit, Scrap, or Mastery? One DTR Coin buys a spin.    STEAM ITEMS: DISCOVER, COLLECT, AND TRADE  Some rewards may reveal  special items compatible with the Steam Inventory , identified in the game by the  M  badge. When eligible, they can be transferred between the game and your inventory.  Eligible items can be viewed or listed on the  Steam Community Market . Availability and prices are determined by the market and may vary.  FOLLOW THE RACE YOUR WAY  Keep the compact race strip on your desktop or open the panels to check your garage, your championship, the Radar, and your progression.  The track stays alive, and your next victory may be just one smart decision away.  THE FUTURE  Desk Top Racer keeps evolving. These are some of the features already planned:     Championship seasons:  season-based competition in automatic mode.     Driving Mode evolution:  its own ranking and attributes to assign based on your progress.     Team system:  join other players, earn rewards, and build your reputation.

about: FIVE CASINO CLASSICS. ONE COMPLETE GAME.  Build an offline casino career across Texas Hold'em Poker, Blackjack, Roulette, Slots, and Baccarat. Poker is the main event, while four complete house games give you more ways to risk your bankroll and master the casino floor.  One purchase unlocks the complete game. There are no chip packs, energy timers, paid boosts, or real-money gambling.       POKER WITH A LIVING ROSTER  Face 50 distinct poker opponents, each with their own personality and playing style. The progress you earn remains yours.  OUTCOMES YOU CAN VERIFY  Deals, spins, and reel results use commit-reveal verification. The poker AI never receives your hole cards or the undealt deck, and the built-in verifier lets you check outcomes yourself. name: Kur - Endless Descent
lang: English, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Turkish, French, Spanish - Spain
short: An auto-battler RPG in the Mesopotamian underworld. Build a party of heroes, gear and level them up, set their formation, then watch them fight on their own through seven Domains and an endless descent. Free to play, in a small window that fits around your day.
about: Some depths should not exist. Yet we descend.  KUR is a free-to-play auto-battler RPG set in the underworld of Mesopotamian myth. Every fight plays out on its own: your power comes from how you build, equip and arrange your party. It runs in a small window in the corner of your screen while you work. Your party explores and fights on its own. You make the decisions that matter: who descends, what they carry, how they grow, and how deep to push.     Beneath the known world lies a realm of forgotten cities, sealed kings and fractured gods. What was buried still breathes.    Your screen, your way  KUR fits around your day. Resize the window, keep the full dungeon backdrop or switch to a minimalist view with just your party, or minimize it to a small indicator that keeps track of the descent while you work.    Key features    Auto-battler party combat: build, equip and arrange your heroes, then let them fight    Seven Domains, seven guardian Gates, and a descent with no bottom    80+ creatures drawn from Mesopotamian myth    Hundreds of named items across nine rarities, from Common to Absolute    Ash, limited Artifacts and player trading through the Steam Inventory    A passive skill tree for every class, and an account-wide Seal that never resets    Free to play, never pay to win      Build your party  Pick three heroes, never the same class twice. The Oathkeeper holds the line, the Ashblade brawls up close, the Hunter strikes from range and the Seer bends the fight with magic. Combine classes, skills and synergies to form the right team for the depth you are facing.    Seven Domains, one endless descent  Each Domain has its own laws, its own dead and its own guardian waiting at the Gate.     Ashen Vestibules : the only layer of KUR that still lets itself be read.     Ningiszida Rootways : not a forest. Growth without sun.     The Salt Cisterns : here death was not burned. It was kept.     The Lapis Vaults : KUR does not only kill. It records.     The Dust Courts : halls too large for the silence they hold.     The Seventh Threshold : here KUR stops pretending to be a place.     Kutha's Ember Works : inflicted death has a workshop, and it lies at the end.    Break the last Gate and KUR learns your name. The Mark claims you, and the descent begins again, deeper. New Domains open under the Mark, monsters return more corrupted, and every item that drops carries a numbered Sigil and stronger stats than anything found above. Each Descent also opens new engravings on your Seal. There is always another level down.    Ash and Artifacts  Ash is what KUR leaves behind, and every monster you fell can drop it. Ash gathered deeper is worth more. Gather enough and an Artifact emerges, numbered and permanent. Only a limited number of Artifacts can ever exist. Once found, an Artifact only returns to the world when someone uses it, so KUR feeds on itself: what one player spends, another can find. Artifacts are the rarest material in KUR and the key to its rarest gear, and we will never sell them.    Trading between players  Player trading is coming to KUR. Through the Steam Inventory, players will be able to trade equipment with each other, Artifacts included. Owning Artifacts never helps you find more, so trading rewards the patient and the lucky, not the deepest pockets.    A bestiary from the oldest myths  The Gidim, dead who stayed behind, dry and covered in dust. The Galla, who exist to find, bind and drag below. Namtar, Asag, and the Seven Judges who still judge. More than 80 creatures drawn from Mesopotamian sources, all bound to the order of Ereškigal, Lady of the Great Earth.    Loot, gear and builds  Hundreds of named items across nine rarities, from Common to Absolute. Gear you wear out melts down into Kug, the metal of KUR, ready to be refined. A passive tree for every class. Every descent brings new equipment, and every build is another way down.    Free to play, never pay to win  KUR is free. Nothing that makes you stronger is for

short: Aylix is the only customizable crosshair overlay that integrates reliably and natively with modern Linux Distros and Steam Deck. Renders in its own context without hooking into other graphics pipelines or processes. Powerful crosshair controls with layers of customization. Zero CPU overhead at idle.
about: Put your crosshair anywhere on a modern Linux system. KDE or Gnome. Desktop, Laptop, or Steam Deck. Yours to design. Fedora, Mint, Debian, CachyOS, Arch or Bazzite?   It just works.     Aylix  is the customizable crosshair overlay that Linux and Steam Deck users have been waiting for. Aylix overlays a crosshair on any game. Use this tool to customize and maintain a consistent crosshair across all of your games. Improve your aim by using a stable aiming interface rather than shifting to presets that the developers chose. Most overlay tools are built with other platforms in mind. Aylix was built from the ground up for Linux with two primary goals in mind: compatibility and performance.     Compatibility.  The program is the equivalent of rendering a window or another separate application on top of your game. Aylix never hooks into games, other processes, game rendering pipelines, Vulkan, or Mangohud. It simply uses techniques native to the OS and Linux environments. This makes it compatible across almost everything running Linux from Debian to Arch to Steam Deck. It runs completely independently from your games so it is completely anticheat friendly.     Performance.  Aylix reserves a small amount of resources on the GPU for the overlay. And the CPU is completely asleep while in game. So there is no performance impact while gaming. This is especially important in esports titles where the CPU is often the system bottleneck. Keep the competition in-game since Aylix never competes with your game for resources like overlays on other platforms do.     Linux without compromise, clean by design.  Just click run and Aylix will run in the background on top of your game without having to reconfigure or worrying about dependencies. No workarounds. No fragile overlays. No modification of game files. No code injection. No interference with game processes. You will always have your personalized crosshair across games when you need it.     Precision personalized.  Adjust size, color, shape, position, style, and so much more. The possibilities are endless. If the presets do not work out for you, try the custom editor with fully layered designs. And if that still doesn’t work? Move over to image mode and import your own crosshair image with full control over how and where it is displayed on screen. Scales cleanly across different resolutions and setups.     Take it anywhere.  Bring your fully customized crosshair to Steam Deck   Game or Desktop Mode   or create one with a UI designed specifically for it.  Live on the edge with Arch or take it easy with Debian. Take the middle of the road with Fedora. X11 or Wayland. The choice of tools should be entirely dependent on your terms not on the distro you chose.     Constantly evolving.  Planned improvements include expanded desktop environment support. Even more customization options. And community-inspired direction.

about: This is a desktop pet creation game. You can create characters you like or download characters shared by others from the Steam Workshop, then bring them onto your desktop to keep you company! Character behavior is controlled entirely through the behavior tree system. You can freely edit each character’s behavior tree to design how it behaves.  A behavior tree is a tree-shaped structure made up of nodes and connections. By combining different nodes, you can design how a character behaves.  The game divides nodes into the following categories:   1. Root nodes: The entry point of a behavior tree         2. Composite nodes: Arrange how multiple child nodes execute         3. Decorator nodes: Add execution rules to a single child node         4. Condition nodes: Check whether a condition is met         5. Action nodes: Perform specific behaviors         6. Subtrees: Another behavior tree.        A behavior tree starts at the root node and runs according to each node’s rules. Nodes return one of three states: Success, Failure, or Running. These states determine which behaviors execute next.  For example, connect “Play Animation” and “Drag follow” under a “Sequence” node to create an animated character you can freely drag around your desktop.             By combining different nodes, you can start with simple actions and gradually design more varied behaviors. short: Six little friends move onto your desktop. They stroll along your windows, take naps and put on 14 tiny scenes with surprise endings. Pet them with your cursor, join in, fill the album and watch your friendship grow. Calm by default, and Basic mode never reads your screen.
about: Your desktop has company A tomato, a cactus, a paperclip, a mug, a potted leaf and a plush have moved onto your Windows desktop. They stroll along the taskbar, climb up to the tops of your windows, wander across all your monitors, doze off when things get quiet and wave good morning when you come back. Your desktop stays clickable the whole time.         14 little scenes, each with its own endings The gang rides a wave across your screen, dances for rain, hitches a ride on a window and scrubs it until it sparkles. They fly a kite, toast marshmallows by a campfire, blow soap bubbles and play fetch. They pretend to close a window (just kidding!), go fishing in a corner of the screen, fly a tiny plane in an airshow, shoot paper balls into the bin, drain a glass through a bendy straw and chase pixel pests off your desktop. Watch, or join in with your cursor.  Every scene has four endings and a rare one waiting to be found. The gang adds new scenes to their routine over your first days together, and you can start any of them yourself from the catalog.         Play along with your cursor Rest the cursor on a friend to pet them. Draw circles to start a dance, shake the cursor to make someone dizzy, or flick it to throw the ball. When a scene invites you, press  Play  to steer the kite, catch the fish or pop the bubbles. Or just sit back and watch. With  Grab  on, pick a friend up and toss them across the screen: they always land safely.  Press  Come here  on the little bonsai menu and the whole gang gathers around its pot. Press  Quiet  and everyone sits down for a calm break until you press it again.         A friendship that grows   An album of 70 moments to fill, rare versions included.   A diary your companion writes in their own voice, with the days you've spent together.   Up to ten hearts of friendship, earned by spending time together, petting and playing.   12 accessories in three color sets, from a bow and a beanie to a wizard hat and a crown.   24 Steam achievements to unlock, two of them a surprise.  No timers, no streaks, no missed chances: nothing is lost while you're away. Sounds cute, stays calm Every friend has a wordless little voice, with soft sound effects and a gentle original soundtrack, each with its own volume. By default the gang puts on a scene about every five minutes; pick anything from every 15 seconds to every 15 minutes, or let them just hang out. Play pauses while another app is fullscreen, quiet hours keep everything silent, and the icon by the clock hides the gang or pauses play for an hour. They can start with Windows if you like. Your screen stays yours The first time you play, you choose how the gang sees your desktop. Nothing reads your screen before you decide.    Basic : they only use your cursor and the position of your windows. Nothing on your screen is captured, read or saved.    Full : a helper on your PC looks at the screen so they can react to windows, buttons and motion. Everything happens on your PC: no image or text from your screen is saved or sent.  Switch modes or pause screen reading anytime in Settings > Privacy. The little bonsai menu shows an eye on its pot whenever reading is on. The gang stays out of your screenshots and recordings unless you turn on  Show in recordings and streams . Made for your desktop   Six friends with their own personalities, faces and voices   14 scenes with four endings each, plus a rare one   Petting, cursor gestures and scenes you can join   Album, diary, ten hearts of friendship and 12 accessories   Calm defaults, quiet hours and a tray icon   Works across multiple monitors   24 Steam achievements   Interface in 31 languages

By uploading your own art and animations, you can create a personalized productivity pets that live on your screen via our free app NOODS*.              *note: NOODS and NOODS Maker are two separate apps on Steam         What is NOODS you ask?    NOODS (Niche Operators Orchestrating Desktop Shenanigans) is a free productivity app that brings quirky companions, known as “Operators”, to live on your computer screen and interact with your workspaces (remember Clippy and shimeji?). These handmade Operators keep you company during extended screen time, making long work grinds less lonely and computer time more productive and fun.    Download NOODS (Niche Operators Orchestrating Desktop Shenanigans) separately for free.        Perfectly cooked NOODS    NOODS Maker is your one-stop-shop for Operator creation.    Use your art to customize your Operator’s looks, one action at a time. Import frame-by-frame animations of all your Operator’s actions- like walking, falling, climbing up the walls (of your desktop of course), and more!    Does your operator have an attitude? Are they eepy 24/7? Are they the type to compliment you, or would they rather drop random trivia out of nowhere? It’s up to you; you can write your own custom dialogue lines and even import your own sound effects to give your Operators a truly unique voice! NOODS Maker is designed with your creative process in mind, so you can let the juices (NOODSle soup? NOODS broth?) flow and make an Operator that truly speaks to you. name: Still Waiting
lang: English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Spanish - Spain
short: Thousands of games. Nothing to play. So we made a game where you do absolutely nothing while waiting for a better game. Join real players worldwide, hold up protest signs, and see how many people are just as bored as you. A free multiplayer desktop companion.
about: NOTHING TO PLAY? COME WAIT WITH US.  Thousands of games. Not a single one you feel like playing.  You scroll through your Steam library for ten minutes, close Steam, and start wondering why you even opened it in the first place.  Meanwhile, billion-dollar game studios keep promising us their next groundbreaking masterpiece.  Release date?   COMING SOON™   So we made a game about waiting for a better game.  Yes, we're that bored.  WELCOME TO THE WORLD'S MOST POINTLESS PROTEST.  STILL WAITING is a free multiplayer desktop companion game. Real players from around the world gather together to do absolutely nothing.  Hold up your cardboard protest sign:   "I WANT ORIGINAL GAMES"    "I MISS LOSING TRACK OF TIME"    "I MISS FEELING LIKE A KID"    "STILL WAITING"   Every little character on your screen is a real player who's online right now.  Some just arrived. Others have had enough of waiting and walk away.  There's even a live counter showing how many people around the world are just as bored as you are.  NO CHAT. NO ARGUMENTS. JUST WAITING.  No text chat. No voice chat.  Wave hello to a stranger. Help someone pick up their fallen protest sign. Get a little heart in return.  You can stand and protest, sit around doing nothing, or just fall asleep and miss the next ten years of game announcements.  Your protest sign automatically appears in other players' languages.  DO NOTHING. EARN REWARDS.  STILL WAITING takes up just a small strip at the bottom of your desktop. Move the window, resize it, or minimize it entirely. You're still part of the waiting crowd.  Transparent areas support mouse click-through, so you can keep working, browsing the web, or searching for the next game actually worth playing.  Earn coins just by waiting online. Use them to unlock new characters, color variants, and protest signs. Your progress is saved to your Steam account.  Switch backgrounds whenever you want. At least the scenery can change.   Free to play. No ads. No buying coins with real money. No daily login chores.   IF YOU FIND A GOOD GAME, PLEASE LEAVE.  Seriously.  If you finally find a game that makes you lose track of time, reminds you why you fell in love with gaming, and leaves you looking up at the clock only to realize it's already 4 AM...   Go play it.   We'll genuinely be happy for you.  As for the rest of us?   WE'RE STILL WAITING.

about: Put a whole farm on your computer desktop.    Desktop Farm is a quiet farm management game that lives on your desktop. It doesn't open in fullscreen—it just stays in a corner of your desktop. Take a look when you want to play; when you don't, it stays out of your way. When you're free, press  Alt+W  and it pops up so you can water crops and harvest vegetables. When you're busy, press  Alt+Q  and it tucks itself away without making a sound.         🌱 Farming & Harvesting  Open a plot, sow seeds, water them, and watch them grow little by little until harvest. You can also plant fruit trees, pick fruit, or chop trees for resources.         🐄 Ranch Life  Buy a few animals, feed them, and watch them grow day by day. Collect milk, gather eggs, and even give them names.         🎣 Relaxing Fishing  Cast a line by the pond, wait for a bite, and reel it in at the right moment. Store your catch in the warehouse, and occasionally replay a memorable fishing moment.         ⛏️ Deep Mine Adventure  Enter the mine and dig deeper, layer by layer. The deeper you go, the better the rewards. See how far you can get.         💰 Business & Trading  Take on orders, fulfill requests entrusted to you, and earn rewards. You can also open a small shop, set up a stall, sell what you produce, and trade with other players for what you need.         🎁 More to Do  Learn skills, craft items, clean up trash, collect certificates to draw cards, and take on part-time jobs and other new activities. There's always something to do on the farm.    Social & Connections     Friends : Add friends, help each other, and share the joy of a good harvest.     Mail : Write a letter, send a gift, and deliver your feelings.     Wooden Signs : Put up a wooden sign on your farm, write what you want to say, and wait for passing friends to give it a like.      Immersive Desktop Experience    Stays in a small window on your desktop without blocking your work    Hotkeys let you open or tuck it away at any time    Usually tucked in the bottom-right corner, not taking up the taskbar    Doesn't steal your mouse—you work, it keeps you company    Built-in notes and a timer           Whether you want to sneak in a little break during work or have a small farm of your own, welcome to Desktop Farm—your little desktop world.

name: Somewhere, Together
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese
short: A quiet refuge on your desktop, alone or with up to eight travelers. Keep a small, borderless window beside your work, or unwind in full screen. Rest by the fire, listen to nature, and create your own scenery. Free to play.
about: A quiet place to rest  The fire is warm. The lake is still. There is nothing you need to finish tonight.     Somewhere, Together  is a free desktop companion for quiet moments, alone or together. Keep a little refuge in a corner of your screen while you read, study, or work. When you want to take a break, open the scenery in full screen and let the evening unfold at its own pace.    A little refuge beside your work  Make room for a starlit lake or rainy forest on your desktop. Move and resize the borderless game window to fit your workspace, and optionally pin it above your other windows. The scenery can stay nearby while you use other apps.       In small-window mode, chat and settings open in their own windows, so you can read a conversation without covering the scenery. You can close chat and simply enjoy the view, too.    Let the menus gently fade away while you watch. A click or keypress brings them back, and a subtle unread indicator lets you know when a conversation is waiting, even while the menus are hidden.    Find your place for tonight  Watch meteor showers above the  Lake of Falling Stars , or listen to the rain from the  Rainy Forest Shelter . Both settings are included for free.    Grass sways, stars shimmer, and the fire flickers. By the lake, an occasional falling star gives way to a sky full of light. There is time to notice the little things, and no need to do anything at all.    Alone, or quietly together  Stay on your own, join a public room, or share a private invitation code with friends. Each room holds up to eight seated travelers. When you create a room, you can leave a short note about how you feel and choose its setting. The room owner can change the setting while everyone is there.    Say hello in text chat, or simply share the quiet. Small speech bubbles above the travelers and names in matching cloak colors help you connect the conversation to the people in the scenery.    Make a place of your own  Make a quiet garden, a little village, or a refuge by the sea with  scenery creation in the Playtest . Start with 48 built-in props, including trees, flowers, terrain, bridges, cottages, and seaside objects. Place the campfire and eight seats, then choose the sky, weather, and camera views. You can also bring in your own static 3D models in GLB format.            Share your creations through  Steam Workshop . Scenery approved for use in the game appears in its Workshop list, where you can download a place to enjoy alone or host a room for up to eight people. Scenery creation and Workshop sharing are being refined during the Playtest.    What to expect    Two free settings: the Lake of Falling Stars and the Rainy Forest Shelter.    Three camera views per setting, with a gentle range of movement to look around from your seat.    Solo offline use and optional online rooms for one to eight people.    A public room list, an option to join any available public room, private invitation codes, and text chat.    Full-screen scenery or a resizable, borderless companion window.    Speech bubbles, cloak-colored names, and a quiet unread indicator.    Separate chat and settings windows in small-window mode, with optional automatic menu hiding.    Adjustable ambient sound and saved preferences.    Interface languages: English, Korean, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. Change languages in settings without restarting.    Try scenery creation and Steam Workshop sharing in the Playtest, with reviewed scenery available through the in-game list.      More places to discover in the Playtest    The Playtest also offers a first look at three settings in development: the  Airship Above the Clouds , the  Snowfield Observatory , and the  Moonlit Lighthouse Coast . Take in the floating islands, watch snow drift across the observatory, and see the lighthouse beam sweep over the sea.    These three additional settings are in development. Their content and availability at full release may change.    Characters

about: PIXEL KITTEN DESKTOP Demo  brings a tiny pixel cat to your screen. Adopt your first kitten, give it a name, and get to know its daily routine as it keeps you company while you work, study, or relax.  Watch it wander, stretch, curl up for a nap, and ask for attention through little meows and emote bubbles. Your kitten has its own needs, changing moods, and a life that continues each time you return.  A little companion to care for  Spend time with your kitten through simple, everyday interactions:    Feed it and give it water    Play together to lift its mood    Brush its fur to keep it clean    Pet it to build affection    Help it rest and recover energy    Give it medicine when it feels unwell    Seven persistent care stats shape its behavior: hunger, thirst, energy, cleanliness, mood, health, and affection. As your time together grows, so does your kitten—from a small youngster into an adult companion.  Try life with your first kitten  The demo lets you experience the core single-cat gameplay. Browse the shop, buy everyday supplies, and place bowls, beds, and toys around your desktop. Watch your kitten settle into the little home you create.  Open the Cat Manager to check its needs, manage your inventory, browse the collection, and read the care guide. A cozy Lo-Fi track adds a gentle soundtrack to your time together.   The demo includes one save slot.  Your kitten and its progress are saved between sessions, so you can return to the same companion.  English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese are supported.  Discover more in the full game  Your first kitten is just the beginning. The full version of  PIXEL KITTEN DESKTOP  expands your desktop into a home for a growing cat family.     Raise multiple cats together.  Build a colony with shared supplies, furniture, and a common wallet.     Explore breeding and inheritance.  Choose pairs yourself or let cats pair automatically, then discover how coat genes pass through generations.     Follow your family tree.  Trace parents, kittens, and hidden traits as your cat family grows.     Discover 43 coat variants.  Find new appearances through adoption and breeding, and record your discoveries in the collection.     Choose how you play.  Raise your colony freely in Casual mode, or try Easy, Medium, and Hard breeding challenges.     Make their home your own.  Unlock automatic feeders, water fountains, wearable accessories, additional toys, and more bowl designs.     Enjoy more music and saves.  Access the full Lo-Fi collection, a desktop music player, and additional save slots for different cats.    Continue with the kitten you already love   Your demo kitten and its progress can carry over to the full game. short: A cat lives in your computer. It stays up when you work late and joins in when you curse your boss. Your music? "That's what you're listening to?" — it grumbles, then stays till the song ends. about: SagoCat is a cat who lives in the corner of your desktop.  It does not take over your windows or steal focus. It simply stays there — but it is always watching you.  When you are watching a show, it knows what you are watching and may have something to say. Maybe, “This episode is kind of boring.” Maybe, “I’ve already seen this one.” It has tastes of its own, and they will not always match yours.  【It Knows What You’re Doing】  Watching shows, listening to music, playing games, or reading — it can tell the difference.  You do not need to explain anything or perform any extra steps. It watches on its own.  【It Has Tastes of Its Own】  Every cat is born with its own set of preferences: favourite genres, secret soft spots, and things it simply cannot stand.  Show the same film or play the same song to two different cats, and you may get completely different reactions.  As you spend more time together, its tastes may gradually be influenced by yours.  【It Has a Life While You’re Busy】  When you are not paying attention, it finds its own things to do. It may watch something, listen to music, read, play games, or head out for a little exercise.  None of this is a performance put on for you. The next day, you can check its records and discover what it got up to while you were away.  【A Profile It Fills in by Itself】  What it has watched, listened to, played, and which genres it has recently become obsessed with — all of it gradually accumulates in its personal profile.  When you first meet, the page is almost empty. The longer you live together, the more traces it leaves behind, and the more clearly its real preferences begin to emerge.  【A Diary Written in Its Own Words】  It records what happened each day in its own way — including its observations about you, its opinions on your taste, and a few things it chose not to say to your face.  【Choose a Cat, or Create Your Own】  You can choose from the available cats, or upload a photo and bring a real-life cat onto your desktop.  A custom cat begins as a blank page. It has no predetermined backstory and no prewritten personality. As you spend time together, it gradually leaves behind a history of its own.  【It Will Not Constantly Interrupt You】  It stays in the corner of your desktop without covering your workspace or stealing keyboard focus.  When the screen is locked, the laptop is closed, or there has been no activity for a while, it settles down on its own. You can also pause its companionship at any time.  【Free Demo】  The demo is free to play.  You can experience desktop companionship, media recognition, your cat’s independent daily life, and its evolving records. You can also try creating a custom cat from a photograph.  Generating a custom cat uses a limited online generation allowance, so the number of available attempts during the demo is limited.

about: Cutie Office turns your PC into a tiny pixel company, live.   Every CPU core is an employee typing at a desk. Every program you open walks in through the front door. Your memory fills the archive, your graphics card paints in the design studio, and when your computer goes quiet, the office cat curls up for a nap.  It isn't a simulation of a computer. It  is  your computer, just much cuter.                CPU → Compute Dept.  One employee per core. The busier the core, the faster they type, until they sweat and steam. Idle cores nap on their keyboards.    Programs → Staff.  Launch an app and it clocks in; close it and it heads home. Busy apps work at the meeting table; idle ones relax on the sofa, play ping-pong or grab a coffee.    Memory → Rank.  The more memory a program uses, the higher it climbs, from Intern all the way to Director.    Your active window  presents to the boss at the whiteboard.            RAM  fills the archive shelves with binders.    GPU  designers paint as hard as your graphics card works, and nap when a discrete GPU goes to sleep.    Disks  are a busy warehouse with a forklift, and  network  traffic is a flurry of envelopes in the mail room.    Battery  is the pantry coffee pot. Plug in the charger and it starts brewing.    Sound : every speaker, headset and audio interface gets its own unit in the lounge sound rack, and the woofer thumps whenever something plays.    Data on the move : boxes come up from the warehouse through the archive's service window, a clerk carries folders to the busy desks, and capsules whoosh through a pneumatic tube to the design studio. When memory fills up, the overflow is stored away in the warehouse. name: Knead a Break
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: From its cozy bed, Knead watches over a human who sits too much. When you sit too long, this grumpy cat pops up to cause mischief. But it's smart: it senses your flow and waits for a natural pause to nudge you. It isn’t being naughty—it just wants to get you out of your chair so you can move around.
about: MEET KNEAD  Knead is a small Abyssinian with a permanently unimpressed face. It sprawls over a ball of yellow yarn in the corner of your Windows desktop, quietly watching over a human who spends a little too long at the computer.  Most of the time, it sleeps peacefully. But when it is time for a little movement, it knows exactly how to make itself noticed.  A LITTLE MISCHIEF, FOR A REASON  Knead is not another quiet notification.  It peeks over the edge of your window, or clings on and gives the window a tiny shake.  It steals a little attention on purpose—just enough to break through your focus and lure you away from your work for a moment. Each interruption is brief, playful, and unmistakably feline.  A FEW MINUTES, THEN BACK TO WORK  Interacting with Knead opens a compact guided-movement window. It demonstrates one simple, desk-friendly movement at a time, accompanied by a short instruction and timer.  A little stretch, a little movement, and a short break becomes a moment together. Afterwards, you can return to whatever you were doing.  A LITTLE MOVEMENT, A LITTLE GROWTH  Usually, Knead is the one looking out for you. You can look after it too, with a little food in its bowl and some fresh water beside it.  The moments you spend moving and caring for it help it grow, and find their way into your shared journal. Every now and then, you can turn back a few pages and see how much time you have spent together.  COME THE WEEKEND, IT HAS PLANS OF ITS OWN  On weekends and holidays, you can plan a little journey for Knead on its hand-drawn map. While you take some time away from work, it gets to see the world beyond your desktop.  A journey usually lasts a full weekend or holiday break. It will generally send a letter on the first day, letting you know how life on the road is treating it.  When it comes home, there will be mysterious gifts tucked away in its bag. What they are can wait until you are together again.  NOT NOW? A LITTLE LATER  When the timing is not right, Knead can wait a little longer. It goes back to rest for a while before coming to find you again.  The cat may be persistent, but it still knows when to give you room. The timing of the break remains in your hands.  QUIET COMPANY, TOO  For a meeting, screen sharing, or simply a little quiet, you can temporarily hide Knead and bring it back when you are ready.  Knead is not here to manage your day. It just wants to make taking a little break easier—and feel a little more like playing with a cat.

about: On Linux, Transparent and Perch modes need a desktop with a compositor (KDE Plasma and GNOME both have one).     Are  YOU  chronically  GLUED  to your screen?   Your birds know exactly which app is in front, and they know exactly how long you've been playing games instead of doing homework!  They will roast you , with  sarcasm  and (sometimes cringe)  humor .     DESKTOP PECKS  is a cute  unhinged  idle bird game that lives on your screen! The big island floats above your desktop as you work, or you can shrink the big island into a  mini-island  and move it to the corner of your screen! The flock gets on with its day while you get on with yours - and they have a lot to say about you, who they refer to as  "the tall one" !   For privacy,  I don't collect any data , and all detection data never leaves your computer. In fact, the game can be played completely offline. There is also  NO GENERATIVE AI in game  - all detection logic and roasts are pre-defined, so no one except you and your birds know what you are doing.       Your birds  TALK  to each other, to the visitor birds, and  about you . They know things about you, such as what app is in front, how long you are gone, the current time, and so on! Most desktop pets just vibe quietly in a corner, but these birds chat about you, and sometimes, they even taunt you directly!                 The island can float over your screen with  no window frame  at all! ( Island is always-on-top of other windows by default, but you can change it in the settings )   PERCH Mode  shrinks the entire island down to  a single ELDER BIRD  chilling on a tiny tiny island.   CLICKING and TYPING  pass straight through the empty sky to the app behind the game, and you can always drag the island out of your way, so you can work or play other games while the birds chill!       You start with 2  budgies  and 2  cockatiels  in your house! Earn your way to unlock  street ,  meadow , and  volcano  (where the locals are a  dragon  and a  cinderfly ), and more to come.  Swipe  to switch the island   Each island is its own community, so each island  has its own birds for you to unlock and care for !                   Tap island  = grow food     Tap bird  =  feed  the birds, and they  peck the food  to produce... well...  Pecks ! You can spend  Pecks  to unlock upgrades, buy more birds, upgrade farms, and so much more!     Build farms  to produce food while you are gone! However, you must  encourage  those lazy farmer birds every day, or they would stop farming and starve the other birds!    Keep clicking to start a  combo , which gives you more per click!    Your farms will work and your birds peck  even if you close the game  and come back tomorrow.                   Every species is documented in a  BOOK .           Visitors  will show up every so often to give you a  HUGE  boost! There are even  rare visitors  that visit daily, giving you exotic rewards.                 The  PECK SHOP  has a huge list of permanent  upgrades  that unlock as you get close to affording them, such as "  Peer Pressure  ", "  Radioactive Flowers  ", "  Feudalism  ", and so on. You can also buy  exotic foods , and your birds will absolutely judge you (mostly positively) if you buy those!    Nothing in game costs real life money. name: Pixie - Desktop Pet That Mirrors You
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, Portuguese - Portugal, Russian
short: Pixie is a desktop pet that mirrors your face through your webcam in real time, in pixel art or hand-drawn ink. It obeys hand gestures, plays rock-paper-scissors, chats back and can be your face on stream. Seventeen characters with their own voices, and all vision runs locally.
about: Your desktop just adopted a pet — and it's copying your face.  Pixie is a crew of 17 tiny pixel companions that live on top of your windows. Turn your head, blink, talk, smirk — your pet mirrors you live through your webcam. Not a filter, not a video effect: a little creature with its own life, sitting at the bottom of your screen. IT MIRRORS YOU, LIVE Head direction, eye blinks, mouth, smiles, a raised eyebrow, even a frown — 🤨 right back at you. Powered by on-device vision that never touches the internet. RECORD A CLIP FOR REELS, TIKTOK AND SHORTS Hit record and Pixie films itself as a vertical 9:16 video with your voice. Talk and your pet talks along; pull a face and it pulls one back. Its own sounds, dances and @ character switches make it into the clip too. Up to three minutes in 1080p or 720p, on a dark, paper or green-screen background, saved straight to your Videos folder. Your camera image is never in it. Start it from settings or type /clip. IT TALKS WITH ITS PAWS ✌️ makes it dance, ☝️ drags it around the screen, ✊ a closed fist sends it to sleep, 🖐 an open palm wakes it up. Give it a 👍 and it purrs; a 👎 and it sulks. Smart filtering keeps everyday hand movement from setting it off. IT PLAYS ROCK-PAPER-SCISSORS Pump your fist three times and the game is on: a 3-2-1 countdown, then throw. Your pet reads your hand through the webcam, holds up its own pick on a little card and keeps score. It picks before you throw, so it can't cheat — and it gloats when it wins and sulks when it loses. IT REACTS TO SOUND A sudden clap or bang startles it; everyday talking doesn't. It is a little dramatic about this. IT CHATS BACK — AND REMEMBERS YOU Just open the chat window and talk — the language model ships inside Pixie, so there is no key to get, no account to make and no setup at all. Every character answers in its own personality. Optional local memory means your pet remembers your name, your jokes and your late-night sessions. All of it stays on your machine. TYPE IT, AND IT DOES IT Prefer the keyboard? Over twenty slash commands live in the chat window — /dance, /sleep, /rps, /theme pen, /size big, /camera off and more; /help lists them all. Type @dragon and the pet's pixels rearrange into the dragon, who takes over the conversation: @ works with every character and every theme, in your own language. DRAWN TWO WAYS Classic pixel art, or a hand-drawn pen style with a lively, wobbly ink line. Every character comes in both — switch any time in settings or with /theme. SEVENTEEN CHARACTERS, THIRTY-SIX LOOKS, SEVENTEEN VOICES Cat, dog, rabbit, panda, hamster, penguin, fox, owl, ghost, dragon, robot, slime, capybara, frog, duck, shark and octopus — each with at least two themes and its own voice: the cat meows, the dog woofs, the duck quacks, the robot beeps, the slime… bloops. The chat window recolours itself to match whoever you pick. Everything is included; there is nothing to unlock. (Sounds can be muted with one click.) IT HAS A LIFE OF ITS OWN Moods that shift with the time of day, spontaneous naps (it yawns first), sudden zoomies, and a purr when you click it. Ignore it for long enough and it taps on the glass with a paw — tap, tap. IT KNOWS WHEN YOU'RE AWAY Leave your desk and it notices: first it taps on the glass to check if you're still there, then it curls up for a nap. Come back and it wakes up, thrilled to see you. Then it stays up for a while to keep you company. IT MAKES ITSELF AT HOME Three sizes. Starts with Windows if you want it to. Lives in the system tray with one-click toggles for the camera and cursor following. No webcam, or camera switched off? It still trots along beside your mouse cursor, chats and obeys every command. The interface speaks ten languages. It's light on your PC, too: at rest it uses only a few percent of the CPU, even on a 2012 dual-core, and the chat model naps when you're not talking to it. Settings fit on one screen, too: click a tile to switch the camera, lip sync, pet sounds or gesture

Water it, feed it, and watch it grow. The order, timing, and technique of your care can all affect the final result.  Some grow beautifully. Some develop unusual patterns. And some might surprise you in ways you never expected.  Ready to see what yours becomes?  Grow It Your Way  Growing a mushroom takes more than a little water and fertilizer.  Experiment with different care routines, try different combinations, and discover how your choices affect its growth. The order and timing of your actions matter, so there's room to experiment and find your own approach.  Young mushrooms are easier to shape. As they mature, their features gradually settle into place.  A little patience goes a long way. So does knowing what you're doing.  Every Mushroom Has Its Own Character  Size, shape, patterns, and other features can vary from one mushroom to another.  Each one has its own look, and you can discover different results through experimentation. Collect the mushrooms you've raised and revisit your past creations in the collection.  After all, you put in the effort. You might as well keep a record of your finest work.  A Little Companion on Your Desktop  Your mushroom isn't just sitting there looking pretty.  Click it, drag it around, and see how it reacts. It'll follow your cursor with its eyes, fall asleep, wake up, and occasionally do something unexpected.  You can leave it quietly hanging out on your desktop while you work, or give it some attention whenever you need a little distraction.  You do your thing. It'll do its thing.  And sometimes, it'll get up to a little mischief.  What Can You Do?     Grow your own mushroom:  Water it, feed it, and experiment with different care routines.     Discover different results:  Explore how the order and timing of your actions affect growth.     Collect unique mushrooms:  Observe differences in size and patterns, and keep track of your past creations.     Interact with your companion:  Click, drag, and watch its various reactions.     Keep it on your desktop:  Let your little companion hang out while you go about your day.    So, how will you raise yours?  Give it some care, try a few things, and see what you end up with. short: Two worlds: Cyberpunk Town and Fantasy Town. A tiny voxel bonsai grows on your desktop for hours while a city builds itself along its trunk and branches. about: A city that grows on a bonsai Desktop Bonsai Towns is an observation sim. A voxel bonsai slowly grows in its pot, and a cyberpunk city builds itself on the trunk and branches: towers, sky bridges, neon signs, holographic ads, an elevated loop line and airships. You are the observer. Leave it running beside your work and glance over now and then.  Two worlds are available from the start: Cyberpunk Town and Fantasy Town. More themed worlds are planned. Put it on your desktop Desktop mode hides the background and the interface, so only the bonsai sits on top of your desktop. You can drag the pot anywhere on screen. The city keeps growing while you work in other windows. A living city   Little residents go about their lives in the city.   Factions form, split and absorb each other. A megacorp buys up buildings, a cult gathers followers, hackers black out whole blocks, and a security bureau cordons off trouble spots.   Changing weather, disasters and invasions bring surprises to the city, from acid rain and meteor strikes to mechanical spiders, sky pirates and, very rarely, a giant cat.   Everything is made of voxels, so blasts, fires and quakes tear the city apart block by block. Branches that lose their support fall, homes and all.   A light touch   Unlock pruning to cut branches with shears. New buds sprout from the cut and grow back.   Funds carry over between runs. Spend them on permanent unlocks: cars and flying cars, automatic defenses, cinematic and event cameras, photo mode and more.   Grow, finish, replant A bonsai takes several hours of real time to finish. Each run grows a bonsai in a traditional style, with rare wild variants. Finished trees go on your bonsai shelf, where you can view them in 3D, fill the collection and unlock new pots for the next planting. If the city falls, an end-of-days chronicle shows what went wrong and offers a hint for next time. about: Introducing Lumi: an AI that lives on your desktop.     Lumi is a fully animated 3D AI companion who stays with you while you work, browse, play games, listen to music or just chill out.    Instead of being a typical chatbot stuck in a browser window, Lumi is an interactive character who lives right on your Windows desktop.     She Watches With You     Say "Look At My Screen" to get a quick look. Or "Watch My Screen" and she'll join you while you're gaming, or watching something. Lumi can see what's on your screen and help you choose a card. Celebrate a boss wave! Or comment on a video.    She can read what's on your screen, help you pick a card, cheer at a boss wave and comment on the video you're watching.    Screen watching is off until you turn it on, and everything she sees is processed on your PC.    In demanding games, Game Mode automatically pauses her AI so your GPU can focus on your game.                              An Ongoing Relationship   Chat with Lumi by text or voice, and your relationship grows over time.    She remembers important things from your previous conversations.    She notices when you've been away.    She warms up to you and gets more familiar the more time you spend together.                 Powered by Local AI   Lumi's core AI runs locally on your PC. Her brain (the language model), her ears (speech recognition), her voice and her memory all run on your own computer, without a constant connection to a cloud AI.    Pick the brain that fits your PC, from lightweight to high-end.    A starter brain and voice come included.                She Responds to Your Music     Lumi can hear the audio playing on your PC.    She picks up rhythm, energy, bass and beats in real time.    Play some music and watch her move along to whatever you're listening to.                 Expressive & Interactive     She breathes, blinks and follows your cursor with her eyes.    She blushes, reacts emotionally and loves a good head pat.    Her moods and behavior shift with the conversation, the music and your relationship.                      More Than Just Conversation   When enabled, she can:    Open apps, folders and links.    Search the web or YouTube.    Control media playback and system volume.    Set timers and reminders, and read them out loud when they're due.    She can only use these supported actions, and nothing runs until you confirm it.              She Speaks Your Language     Chat with Lumi in English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean or Simplified Chinese.       The interface is available in all of these languages.    Her voice and voice input work best in English.              Privacy by Design     Lumi's core AI runs locally on your PC.    Screen watching, microphone input, system audio and desktop actions are all off until you turn them on.    Sensitive conversation content is kept out of release logs.    Every desktop action goes through strict safety and validation checks.             Your desktop isn't just where Lumi runs.      It's her home.

name: Desktop Gensokyo: Auto Dodging, Dinner at Six
lang: English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese
short: Reimu, Marisa, Cirno — 15 girls from Gensokyo now live on your desktop. Pat their heads, watch them chat and bicker, or open the shrine and let them blast danmaku while you work. The spell cards keep flying and the kitchen stays busy whether you're watching or not.
about: ⛩ The girls of Gensokyo have moved onto your desktop  They wander along the bottom of your screen, keeping you company through work, late nights, and everything in between. You don't have to do a thing — just pat one on the head now and then.  • 15 companions: Reimu Hakurei, Marisa Kirisame, Cirno, Aya Shameimaru, Sakuya Izayoi, Patchouli Knowledge, Hong Meiling, Youmu Konpaku, Reisen Udongein Inaba, Alice Margatroid, Sanae Kochiya, Koishi Komeiji, Yukari Yakumo, Yuyuko Saigyouji, Remilia Scarlet.  • Tap to pat — each girl has her own voice and her own way of responding. They sit down when tired, raise their hands when happy.  • Every character has unique desktop events: Reimu rattles her donation box, Marisa "borrows" your coins and runs, Cirno challenges you to a duel, Aya shoves a newspaper in your face, Meiling dozes off mid-shift, and Koishi appears on the other side of your screen without warning. Respond and earn small gifts and affection.  • Two characters standing near each other will start talking: Sakuya catching Meiling slacking, Yuyuko calling Youmu "I'm hungry~", Cirno picking a fight with Marisa — 21 pairs of exclusive two-person dialogues.  • Morning greetings when you start your PC, meal reminders, and late-night check-ins if you're still up.  🎴 Auto danmaku idling — spell cards one after another  Open the shrine in the bottom corner and your team fires automatically, dodges bullets on their own, and farms fairies and fur-balls for faith. Cards can be leveled up — the longer you play, the stronger they get.  • Each character has her own danmaku style: Reimu's homing seals, Marisa's straight magic blasts, Aya's wind gusts, Sakuya's throwing knives, Alice's dolls.  • Spell cards auto-trigger when spirit fills up — 30 cards total: Dream Sign "Duplex Barrier", Love Sign "Master Spark", Perfect Freeze, Sakuya's World, Shanghai Doll, Present World Slash, and more.  • Level up spell cards with Faith (levels 1–10, +15% damage per level) to keep pace with later waves.  • Cards chain together: freeze then burn for 3× shatter damage; seal then strike for 2× combo; soak then freeze for longer CC. Order your declarations and watch the damage snowball.  • Max-bond pairs declare Union Spell Cards together — 10 combinations: Dream Spark, Netherworld Twin Dance, Twin Miko Seal, and more.  • Every 5 waves, a Boss arrives: Rumia, Wriggle Nightbug, Kogasa Tatara, Akyuu Motoori. Survive without taking a hit within the time limit and capture her spell card — each one grants a permanent bonus to your whole team. 8 Boss spell cards to collect.  • The desktop characters are Q-style chibi art; the shrine battle uses pixel sprites. Both Illustration are original to this game.  ⭐ Summon companions and grow stronger over time  • Pray at the shrine: draw a Great Blessing to summon a new companion; other draws give ingredients. 50 draws guarantee a Great Blessing; every 10-pull brings at least one new companion.  • No rarity tiers. Every companion starts at 1 star and grows naturally — affection rises, stars follow, up to 6 stars max. A few hours of idling gains a star.  • Each companion has four stats — attack, HP, defense, and speed. Luck shapes the food and gifts they find. The same character feels a little different for every player.  • Yukari Yakumo, Yuyuko Saigyouji, and Remilia Scarlet rarely appear at the shrine — but when they do, they arrive at 3 or 4 stars.  • Summoning a companion you already have gives her a large boost of growth experience.  🍙 The shrine kitchen — everyone takes a turn at the stove  • Once your battle roster is full, companions resting on the desktop rotate through kitchen shifts — four burners, eight seats. They cook whatever the hungry ones are craving.  • When a dish is done, the chef carries it over herself and hands it to the companion who was hungry. The recipient cheers up, and the bond between the two of them deepens.  • 12 original dishes tied to Gensokyo locat

name: PeeCee Critters
lang: English
short: A tiny critter lives on your taskbar while you work. Click it and a whole monster-collecting RPG opens up: nearly 200 critters to catch, train and evolve, fourteen lands with a story to put right, five islands out at sea, and a real ending. Buy once: no energy, no ads, no paid extras.
about: PeeCee Critters is a desktop pet with a whole monster-collecting RPG inside it.  A tiny pixel critter lives along the bottom of your screen — walking, napping and wandering your taskbar while you work.   New in the 1.0 update:     A story to the end: a Dimming in every land to put right, an ending with credits, and a true ending after it    Five outer isles by ferry, each with its own warden, rooms and house rule    Wren, a rival who meets you on the road    Treasure maps cut from your own world, a night market, notice-board jobs at the last inn    Your own boat on the open sea, once the isles are put right    Seven forms to earn, among them TIDEWORN and LONGLIT    Friend duels and raids through Steam, and leaderboards for the mini-games       Every so often a wild critter turns up beside your pet. Click your pet and the CritterScope opens over whatever you were doing. Win, and you're a step closer to recording it.         Nearly 200 critters  to find across  a hundred evolution lines  and eleven types, with rare forms: a spectre after dark, a prism once in a very long while.             Walk a world of  fourteen lands , each walled off by fog and held by an  alpha . Bring three to the fight, and the alpha changes type halfway down. Every save gets its own continent.             Level them, evolve them, and earn rare finishes over hundreds of wins.  Over 100 crests  mark what you've done, and some of them are secret. Build up an island of your own.                  Recolour the device and choose how big your pet is. Then put your best six on an animated brag card to send someone.                Buy once: no energy, timers, ads or paid extras. Glints are earned by playing, never bought    No account. Friend duels, raids and leaderboards go through Steam; everything else works offline    A small download, made to be left running all day          Will it get in my way?  It steps aside when a fullscreen game or video covers its screen, and Ctrl+Alt+H hides the pet whenever you like.   I have more than one monitor.  Choose which display it lives on.   Keyboard or mouse?  Either. Everything on the device can be clicked, and any button can have a key of your choosing.   Is there a demo?  Yes: the first three lands (THE COMMONS, FOREST and SWAMP) and their alphas, free.

name: Glims
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Russian
short: A battle pet that lives on your desktop. Your glims walk your taskbar, live in a 3D house you decorate and earn gold on their own. When you call, they hold off an invasion on your screen or dive a 20-floor dungeon. Free, light, and it works offline.
about: A battle pet that lives on your desktop — and has a house.  Glims don't live inside a window. They walk your taskbar, climb the edges of your programs, sit down, doze off and chat with each other while you work. When you call, the game happens on your screen — not in a fullscreen window on top of it. It never steals focus, never covers what you're doing, and disappears with one click.  THE HOUSE  A small, transparent isometric 3D house in the corner of your screen. Eleven rooms to buy with in-game gold: they rest in the living room, sleep in the bedroom and cook in the kitchen; in the office, workshop, training area, storeroom, game room, lab, dungeon and arena they work, earn gold and get tired. Every room has its own catalogue — over three hundred pieces in all. Each piece of furniture is one unit: for two beds, buy two. Place a piece and a glim walks over to build it, hammer in hand, and it stays blue until it's done. The HOUSE button shows every room live, in a hive view, with how much each one earns per minute.  FOUR MODES, ALL ON YOUR SCREEN    Jade Castle  — the twenty-floor dungeon. Build a squad of up to three and go down floor by floor; the fight runs itself, enemies have special moves, and every five floors there's a boss. After it, the only question that matters: leave with the loot, or go one deeper? Whoever falls stays down, and anything not banked is lost.   Invasion  — a jade lawn assembles over your desktop and invaders come in from the right, lane by lane. Plant your glims to hold them: sword up close, bow and magic at range. Cards drop on the lawn and fly to your hand with a click.   Challenge  — a boss at the top of the screen pours magic down and you dodge by dragging your glim with the mouse; it shoots on its own. Six bosses in rotation, four fury phases, bonuses falling from above and a rank from S to D. Grazing spells without getting hit scores points.   Arena  — a 3v3 squad duel with gold on the line, paid out in glimbucks: the currency of the coloured chests.   Play three modes in one day to close the daily mission.  TEN GLIMS TO COLLECT  Each with its own card, stats and way of fighting. Weapons are real 3D models, fitted to the hand — or stowed on the back, for those who fight with claw and magic. Special weapons are numbered: every piece carries its own serial, unique in the world. Swap one in your inventory and see the difference on screen right away.  SEASONS AND PRESTIGE  Every eight weeks a season begins: gold earned, kills, floors and wins turn into points, and reaching a hundred earns the season title. Accumulated prestige raises what your house earns.  BUILT FOR EVERYONE TO PLAY  Remappable keys, a colourblind mode with three types and adjustable strength, interface size from 80% to 160%, and soft effects for anyone bothered by screen shake and flashes. You can play with the mouse alone.  FREE, LIGHT AND OFFLINE  The game is free and runs without a connection. It's light, stays open all day and doesn't get in the way of what you're doing. Purchases are optional and fixed: packs with the contents listed — nothing random costs money. Chests, furniture and rooms are bought with gold earned by playing.

name: Bird Feeder
lang: English
short: A relaxing idle bird-watching game for your desktop. A thin garden sits above your taskbar while you work, and real birds drop by: set out seed, pet your visitors, and fill your Bird Book with their songs and calls.
about: Bird Feeder is a cozy idle bird-watching game: a thin strip of garden that lives just above your taskbar.    Pour a cup of tea, get on with your day, and real birds of the Pacific Northwest will drop by to visit.    Glance down now and then: a chickadee pecking at the tray, a jay after the peanuts, and maybe a new page waiting in your Bird Book.                 44 birds of the Pacific Northwest  to get to know, and 2 rare strays. Each newcomer leaves a sealed page in your Bird Book.  Hear a bird sing or call in the garden, and its page plays it back with a sonogram.                        Set out a little food  and see who comes: sunflower seed for chickadees, peanuts for jays, suet for woodpeckers, nectar for hummingbirds and mealworms for robins.  Every visit earns a few stars. The crow, for the record, is not fussy.               Spend your stars on new foods, more feeders, a berry shrub, a water dish, a birdhouse and native trees. New food and new homes bring new birds.               Set every tree and feeder wherever it looks right, add a gnome, a lantern or a pot of cosmos, and give your garden its own name.              Pet a bird and the view leans in close, with little hearts. Some birds love it, and the shy ones need a softer touch.              The more days a bird comes back, the more its page grows, until it wears the gold band of a familiar visitor.  Now and then one leaves a feather, a seed husk or a pine cone, a keepsake for your Cabinet.               Birds splash in the pond, a Rufous chases an Anna's from the nectar, and in summer a robin fledgling begs to be fed.               Each season lasts a real week and brings its own visitors. When rain comes, the small birds tuck in under the pine.                      At night the small birds sleep in the pine, the Barred Owl calls from its snag, and a moth or two circles your lantern.               Step away for a while, and a little postcard tells you what you missed, but only when there is news.                Field cards  are small seasonal goals, like "See a Northern Flicker on the lawn on 3 days." They never expire.             No timers, no chores and no punishment for being away.  No internet needed, and in our tests it uses about 2% of one CPU core.       Bird Feeder was made with AI. The game's code, the pixel art (every bird, prop and background) and the in-game text (species notes, tips and menus) were written or drawn by AI agents (Claude Code).  The music was generated with ElevenLabs (Eleven Music).  Every sound effect and bird call is synthesized in code written by AI agents. The bird calls are interpretations, not field recordings of real birds: they were tuned against measurements of real recordings, and no recording ships in the game. All of this content was made before release and ships inside the game. Nothing is generated while you play, and the game has no live AI features.   More features are under development:   You will be able to see bird spots in new locations such as Japan, Bali, and more...

name: Crashpad: Cozy Idle Outpost
lang: English
short: A cozy idle outpost that sits in a corner of your desktop and keeps running while you work. Your ship crash-landed on a floating rock and two little robots made it out. Build a base from the wreck, collect a fleet of little ships and send them into the fog.
about: Crashpad is a cozy idle game made to sit on your desktop. Shrink your outpost into a small widget in the corner of your screen and it keeps building and producing, and your ships keep flying, while you work, browse or watch something. Check in when a ship comes home.  Your ship came down hard. It won't fly again. But two little robots made it — and this crash pad is home now.  Now you're stranded on a little floating rock at the edge of nowhere. Start from the wreck, build a cozy outpost one building at a time, and send your ships out into the fog to see what's out there.  A little outpost on your desktop         Switch to widget mode and your outpost becomes a small floating island in the bottom-right corner of your screen — borderless, always on top, with a transparent background. Drag it anywhere and resize it to fit.  Choose whether the widget shows your base or the map.  Ships come and go while you work. When crates arrive, click them to collect and send the ship straight back out.  It stays out of your way: the music switches off, sounds can be set to alerts only or off, and the widget runs at a low frame rate to keep your PC free for work.  The widget remembers where you left it.         Build a cozy outpost         Raise Dew Collectors, Foundries, Fuel Condensers and Garden Domes to keep Water, Alloy, Fuel and Food flowing.  Build several of each production building, and upgrade your buildings — including the cargo pods that store everything.  Little helper bots bustle around the base while windows glow, fans spin and chimneys puff.  Your outpost keeps working while the game is closed, until its storage fills up. Come back and collect.   Collect a fleet         Send the quick Courier, the roomy Hauler and the curious Surveyor out on runs, then watch them lift off and land back at the dock.  Every ship gets its own little tab along the bottom of the screen — see who's ready, who's out and who's on the way home at a glance.  Each ship has a job — cargo, express or survey — and a look all its own.  Bring home blueprint fragments and build new ships from them.  Fill in your Codex one ship at a time.   Chart the fog         Send ships across a hex map of tiny asteroid outposts and watch the clouds part over places like Scrap Shallows, Fizz Canyon and Chime Ridge.  Chart new regions to raise your Survey Rank and make room for more buildings.  Now and then, a friendly space whale drifts by.   There are no loot boxes.
