about: If you feel imprisoned at your keyboard too, at least you’ll have company.      Your keyboard just became a prison Finger Prison is a keyboard-driven incremental desktop companion. Keep it running while you work, chat, or browse, and your everyday keystrokes bring a tiny, darkly comic prison to life. Admit inmates, produce and sell reports, then invest the proceeds in your next equipment build. Type through your day. Come back with a plan. Each key is a cell you can manage. Unlock rooms, place equipment, and watch how one keystroke triggers nearby rooms and other gadgets. Experiment with more than 100 equipment items to turn ordinary typing into automatic effects and chain reactions. Build around placement, elements, and fusion Move equipment between rooms and combine Poison, Fire, Frost, and Lightning effects. Upgrade rooms to fit more equipment and choose materials for fusion. You can leave the prison beside your work, then return whenever you want to refine your little production line. A strange little operation of your own Collect inmates, reports, and evidence. Make the prison yours with room skins, inmate outfits, and surveillance-monitor frames. Cartoon reactions and dark humor give each keystroke a touch of absurdity. Big reactions. Small window. Arrange your build in the full keyboard view, or switch to a compact surveillance window in the corner of your desktop. Background input can be adjusted in Settings.    Single-player: keyboard for action, mouse for managing rooms and equipment.   Keep the game running to progress. There are no offline earnings.   Interface available in English, Simplified Chinese, German, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, and Portuguese.   Contains cartoon violence and dark humor.

about: A cozy luck cat for your desktop Saju Friend is a desktop companion. Boknyang, a small pixel luck cat, sits on a cushion in the corner of your screen and stays on top while you work, study or browse. Clicks pass through around the cat, so it never gets in your way. about: Welcome to Desktop Oasis             Demo Note: This demo focuses on Desktop Oasis's core desktop operation, Inspiration progression, water interaction, and collection experience. Some content scale, long-term progression, collections, and expanded features are still in development and testing; some features described below may not be enabled in the demo.      Turn Your Desktop into a Growing Water World    Desktop Oasis  is a small living water world designed to stay beside you during everyday PC use.  As you type, browse, work, or simply use your computer, you gradually generate  Inspiration .  Spend it to discover new creatures, plants, boats, decorations, and all kinds of curious little things, slowly turning a simple oasis into a richer world.     Use Your PC → Gain Inspiration → Discover New Things → Grow Your Oasis      You Do Your Thing. It Keeps Growing.   You do not need to stare at the game or click constantly.  Desktop Oasis can quietly stay beside your desktop and continue progressing while you work, study, browse the web, or handle other tasks.  Come back whenever you feel like playing.  See what you have gained, unlock something new, rearrange the world—or simply do nothing and watch little things drift across the water.               The Water Is Not Just a Background   The water here does more than look pretty.  Boats, logs, rafts, creatures, and other floating objects can drift, move, collide, and interact with the surrounding world.  Drag objects into the water, change their position, watch them move with the surface, or place different objects together and see what happens.  These small physical interactions make Desktop Oasis feel more like a living miniature water world than a looping animated wallpaper.               From Open Water to Your Own Oasis   As you keep discovering new content, you can gradually obtain more creatures, plants, boats, decorations, environmental objects, and special collectibles.  Place what you like in the world, adjust the layout and viewpoint, and let the same body of water slowly become your own.  The world is not packed with everything from the beginning.   Filling it is part of the progression.                Discover, Collect, and Complete Your Encyclopedia   As your world grows, there are always more things left to discover.  Unlock encyclopedia entries, find less common content, hunt for rare collectibles, and gradually fill out the world.  Every new discovery adds one more piece to your oasis.  Some special discoveries can also become Steam Inventory collectibles, extending part of your collection beyond the oasis itself.               It Can Be a Game—or Simply Stay Beside You   You can actively arrange, interact, and collect, or use Desktop Oasis as a long-running desktop companion.  It can run beneath your desktop, and it also supports windowed, borderless, and fullscreen presentation.  Watch the water move,  listen to ambient sounds or white noise,  drop in now and then to see what has changed,  or simply let it stay quietly beside you while you work or study.  The game also includes a dedicated low-resource mode for background use, designed to reduce system resource usage during long sessions.  It does not demand your full attention all the time. name: Deskside Days
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: A little bunny has moved onto your desktop. While you work or study, it lives its own small life in a corner of your screen, learning new skills and growing. In your free time, dress it up, decorate its home, and browse letters and travel photos. Glance over now and then for a small surprise.
about: A tiny island floats in a corner of your desktop, and a little bunny lives there. It has its own day to get through: busy with this and that, out for a stroll, and off to bed when it's tired.  While you write, sit in meetings, or play other games, you don't need to keep an eye on it or plan its day. Glance over when you're done and see how its day went.  You do your thing. It does its own.               This bunny can't sit still. It picks up new skills and keeps practicing, getting a little better each time. One moment it's busy at the stove, the next it may be off to the water with a fishing rod.  You don't have to teach it step by step or stay by its side. Just check in now and then to see what it's been practicing and how far it's come. Small skills add up over time. The bunny's in no hurry, and you don't need to be either.               This part is up to you. Furniture indoors and out can be placed and rotated freely: lay a rug by the window, put the piano next to the bookshelf, fly a kite above the yard. No need to finish in one go. Change a little whenever you feel like it, and the island slowly becomes the place you want.       Its look is yours to decide too. Mix and match hats, backpacks, tops, shoes and accessories, and choose a fur color such as snow white, cream, cocoa or mist gray. Put sunglasses on it and it will carry on with its day, not the least bit shy.               Most days on the island are ordinary. But one day you might look up and catch a spirit rising from the pond, and some nights the bunny heads off to the Dragon Palace.  They don't announce themselves. If you happen to see one, stay and watch for a bit.            Neighbors drop by for a visit and write to the bunny after they go home. These friends are all characters in the game, so there's no friend list to fill and nobody to wait for online.  The bunny keeps a diary, and the calendar records the days as they pass. It also travels to gardens, the seaside and pastry shops, takes photos with friends and keeps them in an album. Flip through it after a while and you'll find the island has collected quite a few stories.               Cherry blossoms in spring, summer nights made for looking up, autumn leaves across the yard, winter snow blanketing the island. Day and night each have their own look. The island changes with the days, and as long as you keep it open, it will share them with you.  When you finally look up from your work, it may have just finished too.

about: Lowtown is a tiny pixel-art village that lives right above your Windows taskbar. It is a fully autonomous desktop companion: you don't build anything and you don't give orders. The villagers live their own lives — just glance down now and then to see what they are up to.         A village that lives on its own  Villagers chop wood, fish, farm, bake bread, forge tools and put up new houses. The village council decides who takes on which trade as the settlement grows, and a little thought bubble pops up whenever someone starts something new. Children play outside, and newcomers arrive from beyond the edge of the screen.          From the first tents to skyscrapers  The settlement grows through seven eras — from a camp around a campfire to a village, a town, an industrial city and finally a metropolis. Canvas tents give way to timber cottages, brick houses and towers of steel and glass. When the whole strip is lined with skyscrapers, the town celebrates with fireworks — then you can start a new world or let the city live on.  Days, nights and seasons  A day passes in 24 minutes: the sun and the moon cross the sky, windows light up in the evening, and the village falls asleep at night.          A year lasts just 12 days. Spring blossom, summer greenery, autumn leaves and winter snow follow one another. Winter is the hardest season: villagers stock up on firewood and food, and children have snowball fights.         Stays out of your way    Clicks pass right through the village. It never takes focus and doesn't show up in Alt+Tab.    The village fades out when your cursor comes close.    Everything is in the tray icon: show or hide the village, choose the monitor, change the speed and language, start with Windows.    Light on resources: low frame rate, below-normal priority and Windows efficiency mode.    Your village is saved automatically.    Cozy by design  No combat, no disasters, no deaths and no way to fail. A hard winter only slows the village down — it never punishes you. Lowtown is made to keep you quiet company for hours while you work or study.

about: Wonder Garden is a little garden that lives on your desktop, right over your wallpaper and next to the things you do every day. Draw a few shelves, drag a seed from your pouch, and your garden starts to grow while you work, study or just relax.                   Plants grow in real time, over days rather than minutes (your very first one grows up within an hour, to say hello). Water a plant when it asks, and grown plants earn coins for new seeds, pots and decorations. Forget about it for a while? It wilts, but nothing ever dies: water it and it comes back.                   Every seed carries its own genes, so no two plants are ever the same: hydrangeas in twelve colours, lilies with freckles or ruffles, a fern that unrolls copper fronds, a poinsettia that turns red for Christmas by your calendar. Collect every form and colour in the Garden Almanac – and share a seed code so a friend can grow exactly your plant.                   Raise caterpillars into seven species of butterflies that drink from your flowers and bask on the leaves. Brush a mimosa and it folds its leaves; touch a Venus flytrap twice and it snaps shut. Now and then a rare guest drops by – a ladybird, a hummingbird hawk-moth, a snail on a damp night, fireflies on a summer evening.                   Draw shelves anywhere on your desktop and dress them up: dozens of pots in ceramic, stone, brass and rattan, hanging planters, string lights, little books, a sleeping cat, a candle that really flickers, a grow light for faster growth.                   On Windows and macOS your garden lives on shelves you draw yourself. On macOS your plants can also settle right on top of your desktop widgets. The garden rests when nobody is looking and has a power-saving mode for laptops.                     A relaxing idle garden that lives on your desktop – no timers to race, no fail state    14 hand-crafted 3D plant species that grow over real days, each one unique    Seven butterfly species to raise from caterpillars, plus rare garden visitors    Shelves you draw yourself, dozens of pots, hanging planters, string lights and ornaments    A beautiful Garden Almanac of every form and colour you discover    Seed codes to share your favourite plant with friends    Seasonal surprises: a Christmas tree in December, plants that follow the real calendar    Windows and macOS; on macOS plants can also grow on your desktop widgets    Monstera, Dracaena and the bee house are part of the separately sold Supporter Pack and are not included in the base game.

short: Your favorite character, living on your desktop: above your wallpaper, behind your apps. Pin GIFs to your game, cut out backgrounds in one click, pick from 10 cursor effects, and grab clocks, visualizers, system monitors and a desk pet. Every click goes straight through.
about: Your desktop, but it's yours now Drop a GIF of your favorite character onto your screen. Scale it, spin it, fade it, park it on the edge of your monitor. Then forget the editor exists. It just lives there.  Images, GIFs and videos. As many as you want. Across every monitor you have.  And your mouse never notices. Every overlay is click-through, always. Nothing steals a click, nothing gets in the way of a double-click on a desktop icon.         On your wallpaper. Behind your apps. Every overlay picks a layer.   On top  floats above everything, taskbar included.  Desktop  sits right on your wallpaper and desktop icons, animated wallpapers too, and slides under every window you open. Your character hangs out on the wallpaper. Open a browser and it tucks in behind, like a real part of the desktop.  Colors clash with your setup? Every overlay has a Color section. Pick any hex tint and choose how it lands: Recolor, Hue only, Multiply, Screen, Overlay or Soft light. Then push hue, saturation, brightness, contrast, blur and film grain until it matches. It's alpha-aware, so it recolors the character, not a box around it. Stick it to a game Click any app and pin an overlay to it. Move the window, the overlay follows. Minimize it, cover it, and the overlay disappears with it. Flip on "only when fullscreen" and it only shows up when the game goes big.  A mascot riding the corner of your game. A frame hugging your editor. A reminder that only appears while one specific program is up.  Want it the other way around? "Only show on desktop" keeps an overlay for when you're looking at your desktop, and "Hide on fullscreen" clears the screen whenever a game takes over.         Backgrounds? Gone. Found the perfect GIF but it's stuck in a gray box? Cut it out. Background removal runs right on your PC, no uploads, with a General model for photos and an Anime model for characters and illustrations.  It works on images, GIFs and videos. Animated in, transparent animation out.         It hears your music Overlays can read the sound coming out of your PC and move with every beat. They know what's playing too: title, artist, album and cover art.  Three to start with:    Vinyl Now Playing : a record that spins up when your song plays and coasts to a stop when you pause, with the album art on the label. The card tints itself to match the cover and the grooves catch the beat. Run it as the Classic card, a Turntable with a tonearm that tracks the song, a Compact bar, or Record only.    Lyrics Ticker : synced lyrics lighting up word by word. Keep it as a one-line ticker above your taskbar, switch to two-line Karaoke, or pick Scrolling lyrics for the full song rolling past.    Audio Visualizer : bars along the bottom of your screen with peak caps on top. Or a Ring that pulses with the bass, a smooth Curve, or an LED meter. Color it solid, with a gradient, or straight from the album art. When the music stops, it fades out on its own.          Widgets that feel like part of the room Ready-made bundles you can grab, drop on your desktop and tune from their own settings panel.     Desktop Clock : five faces. Editorial sets the time big in serif with the date between two rules. Or go Analog with a sweeping second hand, a Word clock that lights up its letters, Flip tiles, or a tall Stacked poster. Add other time zones as small clocks next to it.    System Monitor : live graphs for CPU, GPU, memory, disk and network, a per-core load strip, GPU temperature and VRAM, and a bar for every drive's free space. Stack it down the side of your screen, run it as a thin Bar, or shrink it to a Compact readout. It shifts toward a hot color as temperatures climb.    Focus Timer : a Pomodoro timer as a Ring, a Bar or Text only. Start, pause and skip with global hotkeys without leaving what you're doing. short: A cozy desktop companion for focus and reflection. Settle into a warmly lit room, use a focus timer, keep a private journal, seal letters for the future, and turn passing time into albums, paintings, and memories to revisit.
about: ☽ After dark, come home to this warm little place.     Choose something you feel like wearing tonight. Write a letter you never have to send. Gently tuck the day into your journal.  Here, you can settle into your own rhythm and slowly find your most relaxed self again.    ─── ✧ ───       ⌂ Feel at home  This is a little world you can step into whenever you like: a woodland path, a welcoming door, a room of your own, the focus room, and the studio. Each corner quietly waits for whatever you choose to do this evening.    A vanity and wardrobe are now in the works. When the game launches, you will be able to choose warm, comfortable everyday clothes for yourself.  It is not about collecting more outfits, and you do not need to dress for anyone else.  It is simply a small ritual of returning quietly as your truest self.    ☕ Follow your own rhythm  When you want to focus, begin with whatever rhythm suits tonight. Start, pause, rest—or simply close your eyes and sit with the timer for a moment. As the night deepens, the room will quietly stay with you.    When focus comes to an end, if a small sense of relief rises in you— "this is enough for today" —then that is enough.          ✉ Write to let go, or to remember  The private Healing Journal is where thoughts come to rest. Write what weighs on you tonight—half-formed worries, things left unsaid, or simply how the day felt. There is no right way to write here. The words do not need to make sense to anyone but you.    You can also write a letter across time: to who you were, who you are learning to be, or who you will become. Seal a letter to your future self until the day you choose; when it arrives, the mailbox will glow softly, waiting until you are ready.    ✦  The Treehole Mailbox  is for thoughts that have nowhere in particular to go. Leave a word, a sigh, or a feeling you don't need to name. It might fade quietly, it might rest here, or it might drift to someone, someday. No expectations. No replies you have to read. Just a place that holds whatever you give it.    ❀ Keep ordinary days close  Moments of focus, fragments from your journal, letters you have saved, and artwork you gradually unlock all gather in the memory album. Leaf through each month's pages and watch the room slowly fill with traces of the evenings you chose to keep. Time becomes a place you can always return to.       ─── ✧ ───     A note from the developer: I am continuing to refine Keeplight's room details and develop an optional feature for anonymous letters that travel slowly. Future letters will travel very slowly, with strong protections for your privacy, your consent, and your safety.      ✦ Add this little home to your wishlist. Whenever you want to return, its light will be waiting for you.

name: Amarillo's Desktop Pets
lang: English**
short: A physics-powered 3D desktop companion engine where crazy ragdoll physics meet living, reactive characters. Import VRM characters, or create your own, and let them live on your desktop.
about: Is this the most advanced 3D desktop companion?  I made  Amarillo's Desktop Pets  to be the  most fun  way to showcase and interact with any 3D character. Here characters feel fully alive and responsive, while still giving you an easy-as-pie way to import and customize your own. All the while making them have the best physics you'll find in any desktop companion!            Be physics-crazy  Have fun grabbing a character. Click on them and toss them around. See how their limbs jiggle and twitch. Push them off balance, make them fall, then watch them get back up and keep going.    Or use the Toys included with the game, like the Bonk Toy or the Pin Toy. And I want this side of the game to keep expanding: I'll work on more ways to mess with your characters, more reactions, and more dumb little moments.                Oh, be-ha-ve!  The default behavior of your characters will keep them moving around your screen, climbing onto your windows and causing mayhem.    You will also see them pushing each other, looking at your mouse cursor, chilling, and tripping all the time. The point is not for you to puppet a character every time you want them to do something; I want it to feel like there is a bunch of tiny people hanging around in your PC, each doing their own thing.    But that's not all, I'm also giving you the ability to change their behavior in-game. If you want them to stay in place for a bit, you can do so, but you can also make be more curious about the mouse cursor or climb your windows more often.    Some of the interactions the game offers are grabbing, pinning, head patting, bonking, and more. The Toys and Behaviors options will grow throughout Early Access.            Import, customize, or CREATE  Amarillo's Desktop Pets supports  VRM 0.x , the format used by a huge number of 3D avatar makers and virtual creators. If you are a VTuber with a VRM model, you can load that same character into the game and have them hang around on your desktop instead of leaving them trapped inside your streaming software.    If you are a 3D artist, VRM support means your own characters can be brought into the game too. Import them, customize them, save them, and let people actually interact with the work you made in full 3D, either via the Workshop or privately exporting it as a single file and sharing on your Patreon. And you might find my own official Blender VRM extension pretty useful for this too, just look for "Amarillo's VRM Toolkit" in the Get Extensions menu.    And while the game was conceived for artists to import their own models, non-artists will have the chance to create their own characters using the in-game Character Creator as well. Shape your character's body, tweak their face and expressions, choose a hairstyle, spawn different clothing items, and more. For those so inclined, you can also import your own textures. Transparency is supported.    Here's the basic flow of the Character Creator:    Create or import an unlimited number of characters    Customize their materials, physics and blendshapes    Add your own custom voice lines / subtitles    Save easily swappable presets    Share them in the Workshop, or as .amaCharacter files              Artistic control  I am a 3D artist too, so I care a lot about how a model looks once it is inside a game. Amarillo's Desktop Pets gives you two visual directions you can switch between whenever you want.   Amarillo Shaders  is my own artist-authored shader family, made to present characters with a stylized, semi-realistic look: something a little closer to the classical 3D look I use in Blender. My shaders give you plenty of options for customizing the look of your character's skin, hair and clothes.   Anime Shaders (a.k.a. RealToon shaders)  are for the anime and stylized NPR crowd. They are feature-rich, highly customizable, and made to look great with non-photorealistic 3D characters. Many other games/software use these too, so you might find them familiar.  Switching

short: A turn-based strategy card game of real and fake antiques. Test your knowledge by spotting fakes, if you wish. Adapt to changing demand and prices, take calculated risks, and finish with the most silver. Between games, unwind with idle collecting: 600+ antique cards spanning ten Chinese dynasties.
about: Antiques were once known in Chinese as gudong (骨董), a term meaning “odds and ends.” In his Thirteen Discourses on Gudong, Dong Qichang describes disparate objects from antiquity brought together as a category of their own, calling them gudong. Another interpretation gives each character a deeper meaning: gu (骨), “bone,” represents the enduring essence of the past—just as bones remain after flesh decays—while dong (董) means “to understand.” In this reading, gudong means understanding the essence left behind by the ancients.  In Antique Dealer, you can collect a variety of distinctive antique cards and play strategic card matches.  Collect         The game holds 600 antique cards from ten Chinese dynasties, from the Xia to the Ming, each with six quality levels.  Leave the game running and a new card arrives every half hour, quietly keeping you company.  The collection can shrink to a single small card in a corner of your desktop, so it never gets in the way.  Every card you collect goes on display in your Antique Codex, sorted by dynasty and quality, so you can browse it any time.   Combine   Drag a spare card onto another spare card of the same dynasty and quality to combine them.  When combining Quality I–V cards, you can choose a card of the same dynasty one quality level higher as your target, with a chance to receive a higher-quality card from a random dynasty instead.  Quality VI cards let you choose a card of any quality from the same dynasty as your target.  Play  When you want a challenge, play the built-in card game and outplay rival dealers with what you know about the cards and a sound strategy.   The Book of Changes says: "When it is time to stop, stop; when it is time to act, act. When movement and stillness each come at the proper time, the way is bright."   For an antique dealer, timing is everything. The largest collection does not make you the winner, nor does one profitable deal. When the dust settles, the dealer holding the most silver wins.         Every antique card has a dynasty, a quality rating and a hidden truth: genuine or fake.  Some cards give themselves away, because their dynasty, name and picture don't match.  A genuine card can bring handsome profits, and a fake one is not necessarily worthless.  You can swallow the loss, take your chances on a buyer who does not know better, expose a fake to drive down its dynasty's market, or bluff a rival into taking it off your hands.  The choice is yours.         Each dynasty has its own independent market level.  A card's market value depends on its quality and its dynasty's current market level. Sales, showcases and exposed fakes, in turn, can push that level up or down.  When a dynasty's market reaches its ceiling, its market is sealed, and all cards from that dynasty are confiscated. Once three dynasties have been sealed, the game ends immediately.      Each game consists of multiple rounds, up to a maximum of 15.  Every round has five distinct phases.   The Five Phases of a Round       As night falls and old wares fill the stalls, you come here to stock your shop.  Every Hidden Market merchant has a distinct temperament and their own rules.  Some sell everything at half price; others offer that deal only on the second item. Some move stock fast, selling only in bulk; others let you take a close look before you buy. Some find all manner of excuses to charge you extra; others specialize in buying back second-hand cards from one dynasty.   Each game brings a different mix of merchants. Cheap does not always mean a bargain, and expensive does not always mean a trap. Study the wares, the merchants and your rivals' choices before deciding where to spend your silver. short: A cozy desktop gardening game with a transparent, movable garden. Grow radishes and tomatoes, queue tasks for a little gardener, harvest your crops, and trade produce for seeds and fertilizer. Your plants keep growing while you are away.
about: Make room for a little garden on your desktop.  Tiny Patch is a relaxing single-player desktop gardening game. A little round gardener in a straw hat walks between the beds, prepares the soil, waters plants, sows seeds, and carries ripe vegetables to a wicker basket. Move and resize the transparent, borderless garden to keep a small patch of countryside beside your everyday activities.   Grow radishes and tomatoes  Tend three connected beds and watch crops progress through their growth stages. Harvest radishes and collect a second crop from your tomato plants. Queue tasks for your gardener to carry out in order. Plants continue growing while the game is closed.   Enjoy the harvest  Pick individual plants or harvest ripe crops across a bed. Feel the resistance and spring of pulling a radish, then watch your gardener carry the produce to the basket. Store vegetables by crop and quality in your warehouse.   Keep the garden growing  Sell stored produce for in-game currency, restock seeds and fertilizer, and begin another planting cycle. Choose fertilizer that improves crop quality or shortens the remaining growing time.   A little countryside companion  Warm illustrated scenery, gently moving leaves, and the gardener's work animations bring the garden to life. Adjust the window position and size, control sound effects, and keep your progress with local automatic saves.  Designed for Windows desktops and mouse controls. The in-game shop uses virtual currency earned by gardening.

short: A focus Pomodoro that eats a tomato as your session burns down, plus five time tools on your desktop: timer, countdown, stopwatch, alarm with daily and weekday repeats, and a 20-zone world clock. Sits at the very back of the desktop and never steals your focus. Requires DeskForge.
about: Time you can see without opening anything  A timer in a browser tab is a timer you forget. This pack puts a focus Pomodoro and a full set of time tools directly onto your wallpaper, where they sit in plain sight, keep running while you work, and never pull the cursor out of whatever you're typing in.    A Pomodoro you can read from across the room     The tomato gets eaten.  A whole tomato at the start of a focus block, down to a core by the end — six stages of hand-drawn art that tell you how much of the session is left before you've read a single number.     One tomato per round.  Finished rounds are tallied as small tomatoes, six to a row, wrapping to the next row when it fills — the day's work at a glance.     Work is red, rest is blue.  The status text changes colour between the two, and during a break the finished tomatoes pick up a yellow rim — you can tell which mode you're in from across the room.     Your durations, not ours.  Focus, short break and long break are each adjustable from 1 to 120 minutes, with 1 to 12 focus rounds before a long break. Defaults are 25 / 5 / 15 and four rounds if you'd rather not think about it.     Two sounds, not one.  Pick a different alert for entering work and entering rest, from a library of 20. Or let it roll straight into the next block silently.     Sized to your desk.  120 to 480 px, with the countdown digits, the upper and lower zones, and the tomato itself each scalable on their own. Opacity from 30% to fully solid.      Five more time tools in the same pack     Timer  — counts up, so you find out what a task actually costs you instead of guessing.     Countdown  — set a target and watch it fall. Laundry, a call, something on the stove.     Stopwatch  — start, lap, stop.     Alarm  — once, every day, or weekdays only (Monday to Friday). It lives on the desktop, so you can see the next alarm without unlocking a phone.     World clock  — 20 zones covering UTC, Taipei, Tokyo, Seoul, Beijing, Singapore, Bangkok, Kolkata, Dubai, Moscow, Paris, London, New York, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Sydney, Auckland, Honolulu and São Paulo. Seconds optional. Put three on the desktop and stop doing timezone arithmetic in your head.     It upgrades your sticky notes too  — in the base app each note reminder fires once. With this pack, any reminder can repeat daily, or on weekdays only.      It stays out of your way    Every tool is its own widget. Drag it anywhere, put several on the desktop at once, or keep just the one.    They sit at the very back of the desktop — no taskbar entry, no Alt-Tab clutter, and clicking one never steals focus from what you're typing in.    They keep running while other windows cover them, and they're there again the moment you clear the desk.      Want the desktop to look good too     Dial Packs  — 28 mechanical watch faces across Dress, Pilot, Diver, Sport and Vintage pocket watches, with a smooth sweeping second hand and a carousel that rotates your favourites on a schedule.     Watch Strap Pack  — 16 straps in leather, steel, rubber and NATO nylon, laid flat under the dial or wrapped around it in 3D.      What you need  This is a tool pack for DeskForge and needs the base app. DeskForge turns a cluttered Windows desktop into something you run your day from: drawers that hold your icons and folders, a right-click in Explorer that sends files straight in, real folders opened right on the wallpaper, and live widgets like this one.    Specifications    Windows 10 (version 1903 or later) and Windows 11    Correct scaling at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, 300% and 400% DPI    Works across multiple monitors    Stored locally — no account, no network needed    One-time purchase, no subscription

name: My Little Farm
lang: English*, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, Simplified Chinese, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Spanish - Latin America, Turkish*
short: Meet your new desk-side garden! Crops will sprout, ripen, and sway at the bottom of your screen while you work or study. Tend them well and your little farm will bloom with new varieties, colors, and harvests.
about: My Little Farm   My Little Farm is a charming crop-growing simulator that sits right at the bottom of your screen, keeping you company while you work or study. Plant seeds, tend your crops, harvest them, and sell your produce to earn coins — then reinvest in new seeds and expand your fields.   Grow Your Crops  Start with simple vegetables and unlock new varieties as you progress — herbs, fruits, rare plants, and more. Each crop has its own growth cycle and market value.   Tend Your Land  Water, fertilize, and care for your plants to maximize your yield. Neglect them and watch your harvest suffer!   Expand Your Fields  Reinvest your earnings to unlock new crop slots, better tools, and field upgrades that speed up your growing cycles.   Magic Facilities  Deploy special farm buildings — irrigation systems, greenhouses, compost stations — to boost your crops and automate parts of your routine.   Flexible Layout  Freely drag and resize your farm strip. Place it anywhere on your screen.   A New Kind of Desktop Companion  The bottom-of-your-screen genre has blossomed into one of the most beloved niches on Steam, and My Little Farm is right at home in it. If you've spent time with Rusty's Retirement — the beloved idle farming game that helped define this whole category — you'll feel immediately comfortable here. Like Rusty's Retirement, My Little Farm is built for the multitasker: your crops tick forward whether you're writing a report, browsing the web, or watching a stream. Fans of Ropuka's Idle Island, Cornerpond, My Little Life, Nanomon: Virtual Pet, and Milly's Meadow will also find a lot to love. Each of those games found a loyal audience by trusting that players want something gentle happening at the edge of their screen — and My Little Farm delivers exactly that feeling, with the satisfying loop of planting, growing, harvesting, and reinvesting.   Cozy Vibes, Serious Depth  The cozy gaming wave has produced some unforgettable titles, and My Little Farm draws from the same well. Players who enjoy Stardew Valley's low-pressure farming loop, the hand-crafted warmth of Fields of Mistria, or the pastoral simplicity of Farm Together will feel right at home watching seedlings sprout across their taskbar. There's something here for fans of Fae Farm's gentle progression, Sun Haven's crop variety, and Coral Island's laid-back harvest cycle too — except all of it plays out in a compact strip you never have to alt-tab into. My Little Farm respects your time the same way these games do: every session, however short, moves something forward.   For the Idle and the Incremental  If you're drawn to games that reward patience and compound growth, My Little Farm belongs in your library alongside Tiny Pasture, Village Tale, Idle Waters, and Fish to Dish: Idle Sushi. Like those titles, progression here is measured and meditative — there's always a next crop to unlock, a next upgrade to chase, a next field to open. Desktop Cat Cafe, Maltese's Fluffy Onsen, Not Monday Cafe, and Bao Bao's Cozy Laundromat players will recognize the same satisfying rhythm: small decisions, visible results, a world that quietly keeps growing even when you look away.   Management and Simulation Fans Welcome  Beyond the pure idle crowd, My Little Farm speaks to anyone who enjoys light management and resource loops. If Tavern Keeper's steady economic rhythm appeals to you, if you've built farming empires in Farming Simulator 25 or Rune Factory 5, or if you spent dozens of hours optimizing crops in Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar — you'll appreciate that My Little Farm distills those loops down to their most satisfying core. There's no combat, no pressure, no fail states. Just a field, seeds, sunshine, and the quiet pleasure of watching a plan come together.   Crafting, Building, and Atmosphere  My Little Farm shares its spirit with the wave of atmospheric cozy games that have captured players in recent years. short: Brokk has set up a tiny forge just above your taskbar. You tap the keys, he swings the hammer. Usually it's horseshoes or cauldrons, sometimes something epic, like a legendary sword. His wife Brygida sells it all in their shop. Together, work goes faster and feels better.
about: YOU TYPE. HE FORGES. Brokk lives just above your taskbar, where he runs a forge and works whenever you do. You write emails or code, and he forges items. Every key you press brings his hammer down. When you type quickly, the furnace glows white-hot and Brokk gives it his all. When you take a break, he catches his breath too. A FORGE THAT KEEPS YOU GOING WITHOUT GETTING IN THE WAY The game is designed to stay out of the way while you work. Typing fuels the forge, and Brokk keeps pace with you. Open the panel when you want to buy an upgrade or check on the shop, then get back to what you were doing. You can move the forge, resize it, tone down the effects or turn off the sound. LEGENDS ARE FORGED FROM ORE It starts with ore, then ingots hammered out one by one, and finally a finished piece: a dagger, a cauldron, a horseshoe or whatever the shop's customers have ordered. Sometimes the metal gleams and something legendary takes shape: Szczerbiec. Excalibur. Mjolnir. There are 49 item patterns across five rarity levels. You can browse your collection in the display cabinet.          A look at the full game's collection, from everyday tools to legendary mithril treasures.  HIS WIFE BRYGIDA RUNS THE SHOP    Brygida sells whatever comes off the anvil. Some customers buy what's on the shelves. Others place special orders and pay extra. You decide how freely the forge spends on ore for new items, from inexpensive copper to the best metal you can afford.         THE FORGE PAYS FOR ITS OWN UPGRADES The gold you earn goes back into the forge and shop. Buy Brokk a heavier hammer or better bellows, and Brygida a new sign to bring in more customers. A whetstone improves your chances of forging rarer pieces, while counter decorations raise prices in the shop. You can speed up forging, increase earnings or save up for the next metal. Just leave some gold for ore.  As your equipment improves, the little workshop changes with it. You can also give the forge a different look by choosing a workshop style.         FROM COPPER TO IRON Start with copper. In time, you'll unlock bronze, then iron. The goal of the demo is to forge your first iron item. Once you get there, you can keep forging and collecting with no time limit.   Your progress stays with you.  If you choose, you can carry over your progress from the demo once the full game is released. You'll keep your collection, forge and shop upgrades, and the resources you've gathered. IN THE FULL GAME After iron, you'll unlock steel, silver, gold and mithril. If you'd like to keep building up the forge, add My Desktop Dwarf: Taskbar Forge to your wishlist and follow the game.   Privacy:  The game counts key and mouse-button presses. It does not record the text you type. Gameplay works offline.

about: nfinite R: Idle Racing   is a racing idle management game tailor-made for car enthusiasts and those who love to sneak in a little gaming while working.  Here, you don't need to tense up and focus on hitting the perfect racing line. Instead, you step into the shoes of a team's gold-medal tuner and mod shop boss. The game perfectly supports  [Desktop Idling]  during work hours, with an adaptive window that sits comfortably at the bottom of your screen. While you are typing code, writing reports, or browsing the web, your exclusive ride is automatically speeding along the edge of your screen with its engine roaring—continuously generating income for you without ever delaying your actual work.  Say goodbye to the heavy grind and tense nerves! No stressful inputs are required. Check in occasionally, click a few times when you're free, and just enjoy the fun of the game.             Development Plan         Tuning & Simulation Management   Start from a dilapidated garage and a beat-up old street racer, and gradually revive your custom car empire. Say goodbye to tedious stat crunching; the game offers the pure soul of car modification. Unlock more modification kits as you level up, which not only drastically boosts your car's performance but also evolves its badass appearance. Hire and manage workshop employees to build an efficient and lightning-fast workflow!            Intense Idle Racing   The cars drive fully automatically on idle throughout the race, never demanding your core focus. During your breaks, you can choose to actively intervene—by training racers, unleashing exclusive skills at critical moments, and pulling off extreme overtakes. Instantly take control of the race's pacing and use your strategy to significantly boost your win rate and tournament earnings.           Deep Modification System   Satisfy your ultimate craving for machinery and speed! Dive deep into your vehicle's powertrain and chassis tuning, from engine enhancements to transmission system upgrades. Not only are there hardcore internal performance boosts, but there is also a massive variety of widebody kits, custom spoilers, and personalized wheels for you to mix and match. Every meticulous tweak allows your race car to show off a truly unique stance on the track.           Collect More Vehicles   As your garage continues to expand, you will have the opportunity to unlock and collect a massive roster of classic race cars across different styles. Continuously enrich your garage collection, assign the most suitable cars to compete based on specific track requirements and personal preferences, and watch them roar past on your secondary screen.           Rich Character System   Recruit and train highly talented racers and tuning shop mechanics. Every driver has an exclusive driving style and unique skills that can save the day on the track; meanwhile, excellent workshop staff and operations specialists can massively improve prep efficiency and offline income. Strategically balance your team lineup to keep your crew running like a well-oiled machine.           Dynamic Weather System   Your racing journey will never be monotonous. The game introduces a rich, dynamic weather system. Whether it's a crystal-clear street or a neon-lit rainy night, the game delivers completely different visual atmospheres, making every idle lap feel immersive and fresh.           Diverse Scene Selections   From bustling urban city streets with heavy traffic to winding mountain hairpin turns, and all the way to endless coastal highways.
